{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZkDP4w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDKslg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 91, "title": "Implement 8259A SNGL initialization and single-mode master interrupt delivery", "body": "## Problem

The shared PIC implementation ignores ICW1.SNGL. `Pic::write` always consumes ICW3, shifting subsequent ICW4 and mask writes when software selects single mode. `Bus::irq` also always treats master IR7 as a slave acknowledgement, preventing correct single-mode delivery.

This is a bounded missing interrupt-controller behavior affecting both VM and Ap. Sources: [initialization implementation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/d793aaf83579e701fdebfe570d374392fc6c8c00/src/devices.rs#L100), [interrupt delivery and physical cascade tracking](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/d793aaf83579e701fdebfe570d374392fc6c8c00/src/bus.rs#L469).

## Expected outcome

Implement single-mode initialization and 8086 interrupt delivery while preserving ordinary PC-98 cascading.

ICW1 bit 1 is SNGL; bit 0 is IC4. Initialization must consume:

| SNGL | IC4 | Sequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0 | ICW1 → ICW2 → ICW3 |
| 0 | 1 | ICW1 → ICW2 → ICW3 → ICW4 |
| 1 | 0 | ICW1 → ICW2 |
| 1 | 1 | ICW1 → ICW2 → ICW4 |

The next data write is OCW1. IC4=0 leaves AEOI disabled. These sequencing rules follow [Intel 8259A, initialization and Figures 6–7](https://www.scs.stanford.edu/11wi-cs140/pintos/specs/8259A.pdf#page=9).

For the supported 8086 subset, the vector is `(ICW2 & F8h) | local_irq`. Normal acknowledgement retains ISR until EOI; AEOI does not retain it after acknowledgement. A single-mode master supplies its own vector for IR7 without acknowledging the slave. See [Intel’s interrupt sequence and vector format](https://www.scs.stanford.edu/11wi-cs140/pintos/specs/8259A.pdf#page=7).

Applying this contract to the repository’s fixed wiring means retaining slave INT → master IR7 edge tracking. A local master acknowledgement must leave the slave request and input history intact; a continuously asserted slave INT must not produce repeated edges. This is a source-grounded integration requirement, not a request to change board wiring.

Scope: initialization sequencing on both controllers, single-mode master delivery, and transitions back to the existing cascade configuration. IC4=0 acceptance covers sequencing and defaults only; MCS-80/85 interrupt output is outside scope.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `d793aaf83579e701fdebfe570d374392fc6c8c00`.

Minimal original Rust reproduction for the Coordinator to execute:

```rust
use pc98_rust::devices::Pic;

let mut p = Pic::new(8);
p.write(false, 0x13); // single mode, ICW4 present
p.write(true, 0x20);  // ICW2
p.write(true, 0x01);  // ICW4: 8086, normal EOI
p.write(true, 0xfe);  // OCW1: enable only IR0
assert_eq!(p.read(true), 0xfe);
assert!(!p.auto_eoi);
```

Static tracing predicts current IMR=00h and AEOI=true: 01h is swallowed as ICW3 and FEh becomes ICW4. This evaluator did not execute the reproduction.

The [existing PIC tests](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/d793aaf83579e701fdebfe570d374392fc6c8c00/tests/pic.rs) cover priority, rotation, special masks, polling, reset and cascaded delivery. Their initialization helpers and initialization-specific cases use cascade sequences; they do not cover SNGL. Preserve these tests and the original PIC/PIT/FDC guest probes. The supplied context lists no open Issues; completed polling and IRQ-edge improvements do not implement this behavior.

### Project progress

PR #90 adds bounded x87 initialization/readback; FPU remains partial. The [Coordinator’s validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/d793aaf83579e701fdebfe570d374392fc6c8c00/docs/validation.md#issue-89-ap-x87-environment-initializationreadback-2026-10-24) reports 357 native and 126 production release-Wasm browser cases passing. The default browser invocation ran zero cases because port 8000 was occupied; the reported alternate-port run preserved both serving roots, assertions and budgets. No independent review or remote CI evidence was supplied. Static inspection identified no concrete recovery requirement from that change.

All 26 inventory scopes remain required:

| Status | Categories |
| --- | --- |
| partial | cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, fpu, memory, pic, pit, dma, rtc, keyboard, mouse, fdc, ide, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, pcm86, bios, lio, integration |
| implemented_unverified | grcg |
| unimplemented | paging |

None is verified. Protected execution, paging and numerical x87 remain required. This Issue will leave PIC partial: programmable ICW3 routing, SFNM, fuller level/spurious behavior, AEOI polling and concurrent polling/CPU acknowledgement remain outstanding. Limited probes and six-game regressions establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

This evaluation used repository reads and an authoritative public specification only. It ran no builds/tests, prepared no fixtures and changed nothing. Missing local assets do not block project planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record the minimal reproduction failing on the baseline and passing after implementation. Add original native tests covering all four initialization sequences above, distinct first and subsequent mask writes, ICW2 alignment and both normal/AEOI ICW4 choices. Exercise both controllers’ port pairs independently; do not assert 8086 delivery for IC4=0.
- [ ] Test all eight local IRQs under single-mode 8086 initialization, using multiple vector bases and checking masks, IRR/ISR, normal EOI and AEOI against the stated contract.
- [ ] On both profiles, test single-mode master IR7 with an otherwise idle slave and with a pending slave request. Check the exact vector and both controllers’ state. Include a held slave INT across master acknowledgement, EOI and subsequent ticks/port operations, then an actual deassertion/reassertion to distinguish retained input history from repeated latching.
- [ ] Cover reinitialization between single and cascade modes, restart by a fresh ICW1 during each initialization stage, cancellation of an armed poll, controller/machine isolation and Machine reset. With fresh quiescent inputs, restoring ordinary cascade mode must again deliver the slave vector and retain separate normal-EOI obligations.
- [ ] Add an original MIT or explicitly licensed source-built guest probe using guest I/O and real hardware interrupt entry/IRET. Exercise single-mode PIT delivery in normal and AEOI modes, plus master IR7 driven by a guest-issued FDC READ ID. Record exact master/slave state before separately draining the slave, then demonstrate restored cascaded delivery. The host must not fabricate PIC requests, vectors or result bytes.
- [ ] Pin the probe’s source/license, assembly command, source/image hashes, independently specified result bytes, guards and execution budget in a checked manifest. Integrate offline preparation into README/CI. Boot the identical image natively and in production release-Wasm on VM and Ap, cold and after reset, at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Require guest PASS without FAIL, exact results/guards, unchanged media and no emulator/browser errors within 2,000,000 scheduler slots per boot.
- [ ] The Coordinator prepares lawful prerequisites using README instructions and runs `cargo test --locked --test pic --test core --test cpu386 --test pit --test fdc --test hdd --test sound86`, then `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check` and `npm test`. Preserve existing hardware, CPU interrupt-shadow, DOS/apps, VM, audio/storage and six-game assertions and budgets. An equivalent isolated-port browser run is acceptable when documented with the same production artifact, both roots, assertions, timeouts and budgets.
- [ ] Update the PIC hardware contract and validation record with exact commands/results and remaining limitations. Preserve existing initialization/reset policies beyond this scope. Use original or licensed source-provenanced tests; no commercial ROM acquisition, copied emulator implementation, unrelated UI/tooling work or compatibility claims.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
